![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096835/assets/2b9aab0fb479571175b957870ceec3bf0c7bf7de026f45333f4f11bb062bc4c1.png)

Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of three line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-1,0]$, the piecewise linear for $x\in [0,2],$ and the piecewise linear for $x\in [2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-1.
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-2.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =-1+2-2 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
